what: Known-answer fixtures for the validation instruments, declared and committed BEFORE any instrument is changed. Each fixture is a constructed input with one stated answer. The runner is validation/fixtures/run_fixtures.py.
origin: the owner's work order 'LID Package A: instrument reliability'; the defects were measured in audit/2026-11-24/LID_execution_results_2026-11-24.md (Stage 01 and Stage 03, repair register R1-R5, R9)
why_its_own_file: registry/DECLARED.json declares the provenance chain and another open branch appends to it; a second append here would collide with that one

F1.input: the command line with --claim no_such_claim on a one-entity index
F1.must_read: verdict UNKNOWN; posterior_probability null; the unknown name is not run as a claim that returns True
F1.defect: an unregistered claim name silently becomes lambda: True

F2.input: one claim function that takes no argument, one entity with 5 scoped attributes
F2.must_read: evidence_count 1 (not 5); the claim is called once; the posterior equals the posterior with 1 attribute
F2.defect: the same claim is counted once per attribute, so the posterior rises with the number of attributes

F3.input: (a) a scoped attribute with one constraint and an ontology in which nothing matches it; (b) a scoped attribute with an empty scope
F3.must_read: (a) the check reads NOT_TESTED, tests_survived 0, falsification_resistance null; (b) 0 counterexamples, falsification_resistance null
F3.defect: no match is counted as survived; with 0 tests the score is 1.0

F4.input: entity A with a link to an id that is not in the ontology
F4.must_read: the result lists the unresolved link (source, target, relation) under 'unresolved', and the tree shows the target as an unresolved node
F4.defect: a link whose target is not in the ontology is dropped silently

F5.input: an index entry whose path does not exist
F5.must_read: the report carries load_failures with state LOAD_FAILED for that id; the thin index entry is not used in its place (falsifier: no analysis of the entity; audit: scoped_ratio null, not 1.0; dependency_tree: the id is not built from the thin entry)
F5.defect: a load failure falls back to the thin index entry without a word

F6.input: a copy of ontology/ and schemas/: (a) as it is, with the allowlist; (b) with one more broken link added; (c) as it is, without the allowlist
F6.allowlist: WOLF_PACK -> COUNCIL (synergy) is declared KNOWN_HELD in registry/known_held_links.json with its reason, so the build passes on that one link and on no other
F6.defect: broken links are printed and the build still writes the index and exits 0

F7.input: (a) a copy of pipeline.sh, ontology/, schemas/, scripts/ as they are; (b) the same copy reduced to ontology/social/, with one record made invalid (id set to a number); (c) the reduced copy with schemas/coordination.schema.json removed, so a $ref cannot resolve
F7.must_read: every case prints a 'Results:' line. (a) exit 0 and '0 failed'; (b) exit 1, a [FAIL] line naming the invalid file, '1 failed'; (c) exit 1, a [FAIL] line naming each file whose $ref cannot resolve, with the exception text
F7.defect: a $ref that the bare jsonschema.validate() cannot resolve raises an exception the snippet does not catch; set -e ends the script with exit 1 and no FAIL line, no reason and no Results line (audit/2026-11-24/LID_review_of_Kimi_rev2_and_pipeline_gate_2026-11-24.md). Reported by Kimi (Moonshot AI), reproduced by the audit.

rules.order: fixtures are run against the unchanged instruments first and the result is committed (results_before.json); then each instrument is repaired until its fixture passes
rules.legacy: the behaviour before the repair stays reachable behind a --legacy flag (and a legacy=True argument), for comparison; it is not deleted
rules.no_tuning: a fixture's stated answer is not changed after the instruments are seen to fail or pass it
rules.stdlib: the runner and the repairs use the standard library only. scripts/build_index.py already imports jsonschema; where that is not installed F6 reads NOT_RUN, which is not a pass
